usamo-usamo-1974-01.prompt: Let $a$, $b$, and $c$ denote three distinct integers, and let $P$ denote a polynomial having all integral coefficients. Show that it is impossible that $P(a)=b$, $P(b)=c$, and $P(c)=a$.
usamo-usamo-1974-01.answer: Since $u-v \mid P(u)-P(v)$: $a-b \mid b-c \mid c-a \mid a-b$, so all three differences have the same absolute value $k>0$; but three numbers $\pm k$ cannot sum to $0$.

usamo-usamo-1974-02.prompt:
Prove that if $a$, $b$, and $c$ are positive real numbers, then
$$a^ab^bc^c\ge (abc)^{(a+b+c)/3}.$$
usamo-usamo-1974-02.answer: Taking logarithms, $3\sum a\ln a - \sum a\sum\ln a = \sum_{\text{pairs}}(a-b)(\ln a-\ln b) \ge 0$.

usamo-usamo-1974-03.prompt: Two boundary points of a ball of radius 1 are joined by a curve contained in the ball and having length less than 2. Prove that the curve is contained entirely within some hemisphere of the given ball.
usamo-usamo-1974-03.answer: Cut by the plane through the center perpendicular to $A+B$; a crossing point $C$ would give length $\ge AC + CB = |C-A| + |C+A| \ge 2$, since the reflection in that plane swaps $B$ and $-A$.

usamo-usamo-1974-04.prompt:
A father, mother and son hold a family tournament, playing a two person board game with no ties. The tournament rules are:

(i) The weakest player chooses the first two contestants.

(ii) The winner of any game plays the next game against the person left out.

(iii) The first person to win two games wins the tournament.

The father is the weakest player, the son the strongest, and it is assumed that any player's probability of winning an individual game from another player does not change during the tournament. Prove that the father's optimal strategy for winning the tournament is to play the first game with his wife.
usamo-usamo-1974-04.answer: With $p=P(\text{F beats M})$, $q = P(\text{F beats S})$, $r = P(\text{M beats S})$: sitting out gives $pq$, and $P_{\text{vs M}} - P_{\text{vs S}} = (p-q)\,[pr(1-q)+q(1-p)(1-r)] > 0$ since $p > q$.

usamo-usamo-1974-05.prompt: Consider the two triangles $\triangle ABC$ and $\triangle PQR$ shown in Figure 1. In $\triangle ABC$, $\angle ADB = \angle BDC = \angle CDA = 120^\circ$, where $D$ is the interior point joined to $A$, $B$, $C$ (so $DA=u$, $DB=v$, $DC=w$ and $BC=a$, $CA=b$, $AB=c$). In the equilateral triangle $PQR$ with side $x$, the interior point $M$ has $MP=a$, $MQ=b$, $MR=c$. Prove that $x=u+v+w$.
usamo-usamo-1974-05.answer: Write $M = (\alpha P + \beta Q + \gamma R)/x$ with $\alpha+\beta+\gamma = x$; then $MP^2 = \beta^2+\gamma^2+\beta\gamma$ etc., so segments $\alpha,\beta,\gamma$ at $120^\circ$ form a triangle congruent to $ABC$; uniqueness of the $120^\circ$ point gives $(\alpha,\beta,\gamma) = (u,v,w)$.
